children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures end Friday's session steady to higher, forgoing earlier losses.

Chicago soybeans and soyoil also turned around today after the United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said there will be an announcement on the trade talks between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday.

In other outside markets, sharp declines in crude oil continued to pressure the vegetable oils, limiting gains in at the Chicago Board of Trade. European rapeseed closed mixed and Malaysian palm oil was weaker.

Weekend weather Going into the first weekend of autumn, Prairie temperatures are to be in low to high teens Celsius. Southern Manitoba and much of Alberta are to get rain on Saturday, while Saskatchewan is to remain dry.
Crush, exports Statistics Canada reported a record August canola crush of about 1.24 million tonnes, which is also the second largest for any month.
The Canadian Grain Commission said canola exports for the week ended Sept. 20 improved to 43,300 tonnes from virtually zero.
The year-to-date rose to 752,900 tonnes compared to 627,400 a year ago.
Loonie The Canadian dollar eased back on Friday afternoon, with the loonie at 70.69 U.S. cents, compared to Thursday's close of 70.74.
Prices There were 59,437 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to 60,187 on Thursday. Spreading accounted for 36,946 contracts traded.
